title: improv·artist · thread (Chiharu Shiota)
mutation_directive: improv artist: thread via Chiharu Shiota

improv_extras.practice: rooms filled with red or black thread; memory webs, suspended objects

v1.feedback: Threads are straight-line segments; adding a single catenary or gravity-droop control point per thread (quadratic Bezier subdivided into 3-4 sub-segments) would dramatically improve the Shiota read — her threads always sag and tangle, never pull taut like guy-wires. With additive blending and base alpha around 0.14, the overhead cross-web and floor threads risk vanishing on most monitors; raise base alpha to ~0.22 or switch the far threads to normal blending so density reads as mass rather than glow. The boat silhouette is solid but could use ~600 hull points and tighter internal cross-thread threshold (~1.2) to build the opaque thread-skin she actually wraps vessels in.

v2.feedback: The Shiota vessel concept is legible — boat hull with radiating thread web — but the threads are too dark and transparent (alpha 0.22–0.35 with premultiplied output) against the near-black background, making the piece read as a dim smear rather than the dense, taut thread rooms Shiota is known for. Raise thread alpha to 0.5–0.8 range and use a brighter crimson (e.g. vec3(0.7, 0.12, 0.10)) so the web density becomes the visual subject, not the void. The catenary sag is a nice touch but the hull-to-hull INTERNAL_THRESHOLD of 1.2 units is too tight for 600 points on that parametric curve — most hull pairs won't connect, wasting the dense-weave intent; widen it or use index-neighbor connectivity instead. Add a suspended object inside the hull (even a simple key or shoe silhouette from point particles) to complete the Shiota vocabulary of memory-charged objects caught in thread.
